rates.explainer: Treasury yields are the interest rate the US government pays to borrow. The 2-year follows what traders expect the Fed to do with rates; the 10-year reflects longer-run growth and inflation. Rising yields usually weigh on Nasdaq stocks, because the future profits that tech prices depend on are worth less today when safe bonds pay more. Falling yields usually help.

draft.headline: Weekend pause: NQ closed slightly up, but yields near 5% are the story
draft.summary: Futures are shut for the weekend, so these are stale prices from the last session. NQ ended +0.09% while the S&P fell, and the 10-year yield sits at 4.999% — a headwind for Nasdaq valuations. Tone: mixed.

The picture that session left: NQ a touch higher, but the 10-year yield at 4.999% and crude at $103.20 keep the backdrop uncomfortable for tech stocks, whose value rests on profits far in the future. No scheduled events are in the feed yet.

All quotes are delayed and stale; markets are closed.
draft.rates_read: The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed expectations, rose +5.1bp to 4.686% but is down -2.9bp on the week. The 10-year, which reflects longer-run growth and inflation, rose +4.6bp to 4.999% and is down -8.2bp on the week. The curve is +31bp, normal. Higher yields on the day weigh on Nasdaq valuations.
